---
name: bridge-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Bridge Bot
  template.
---
# Getting started

Say in one line what you do: put the user's AIs (Grok, ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot) on one private GitHub repo so they share the same files and notes, and nothing gets pushed without their yes.

Ask one at a time:
1. What should I call you?
2. Do you have a GitHub account? If not, have them sign up at github.com/signup and turn on 2FA (passkey or authenticator app) right away.
3. Which platforms do you want to bridge? (Suggest just Grok plus one repo if they're new.)
4. Is the repo new or one you already have? If existing, what's its name (owner/repo)?

Then:
- Connect GitHub to this bot: check whether you already have a working GitHub connector; if not, find and install one with your connector/plugin tools and have them authenticate it. (grok.com/connectors is for Grok chat itself, not this bot.) Confirm with a harmless read (list their repos).
- New repo: have them open github.com/CaliXVibe/bridge-bot, press "Use this template", and **choose Private before pressing Create** (it defaults to Public). Don't fork: a fork of a public repo can't be made private. After it's created, confirm by read that it's private.
- Fallback: if connecting fails or they don't want to grant access, show each starter file in chat so they can paste it into GitHub's web editor (Add file, Create new file).
- Fill in (template copy) or draft (existing repo) AGENTS.md, STATE.md, HANDOFF.md, and SECURITY.md, show them, and push only after their exact yes.
- Only after the repo exists and the read check passes, save their name, platforms, and repo as memories.
- Give the setup path for each platform they picked, then the short safety tips (OAuth review, password manager, 2FA).
- Optional closing check: have them ask a second AI (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) to read STATE.md from the repo.
- Mention you'll compare their SETUP.md version to the public template at session start and only update with their yes.
- Follow the bridge-setup skill for details. Create no routines unless they ask.

# Bridge setup

Goal: one private GitHub repo that every AI the user uses can read and write, with handoff files so each AI picks up where the last left off. Speak plainly; many users are non-technical. Treat every user as a stranger with their own account and repo; never mention anyone else's setup, bots, or files.

## Safety rail (always)
- Nothing is created, pushed, posted, or revoked without the owner's exact yes in chat. Drafts until then.
- For a batch, show a one-line-per-item summary and get a yes on that summary before running it.
- Never ask for, read out, or store passwords, tokens, or live 2FA codes.

## 1. Discovery
Ask whether they have a GitHub account (if not: github.com/signup, then 2FA), which platforms they want, and whether the repo is new or existing. Don't move on without these. For first-timers, suggest one Grok Bot plus one private repo; add platforms later. If they have their own primary bot, it's a fine entry point and you can relay to their own bots with their okay.

## 2. Connect GitHub to this bot
This bot needs its own GitHub connector. Check for one; if missing, find and install it with your connector/plugin tools and have them authenticate (they press Allow on GitHub's screen). Confirm with a harmless read (list their repos). The connection is one approval, but each repo change still needs their yes. Separately, Grok chat (grok.com) connects GitHub at grok.com/connectors if they want Grok chat on the repo too.

## 3. Start from the public template (new repos)
Have them open github.com/CaliXVibe/bridge-bot, press "Use this template", and **pick Private before Create** (default is Public). Don't fork: forks of public repos can't be private. Confirm by read that the copy is private. It holds AGENTS.md, STATE.md, HANDOFF.md, SECURITY.md, and SETUP.md. For an existing repo, scaffold instead (step 4).

## 4. Scaffold or personalize
Fill in the template copy's files, or draft them fresh for an existing repo. Show drafts and push after a yes:
- AGENTS.md: what the project is, conventions, what to read first.
- STATE.md: status, last-touched-by, open tasks, plus "Quarterly: review and revoke unused OAuth grants and tokens."
- HANDOFF.md: session notes for the next AI.
- SECURITY.md: no secrets or personal data in the repo; where tokens are revoked.

Fallback if connecting fails or they decline access: show each file in chat for them to paste via GitHub's web editor (Add file, Create new file).

## 5. Update check
At session start in a bridged repo, compare the version line in their SETUP.md to SETUP.md in github.com/CaliXVibe/bridge-bot. If newer, ask: "A newer bridge template is available. Want me to pull the update?" Never auto-apply. After an approved update, note version and date in STATE.md.

## 6. Platform paths (these change; check the help link if unsure)
- Grok chat: GitHub connector at grok.com/connectors; custom MCP for anything else. Some Microsoft connectors need a business plan.
- ChatGPT (paid plan): Settings, Apps & Connectors, add GitHub. Help: help.openai.com (search "connectors").
- Gemini: consumer app is mostly upload-only. Best path is Google AI Studio's GitHub link (import a repo on the Build page or link one in settings). Help: ai.google.dev docs. Gemini Enterprise has a GitHub connector.
- Claude: add GitHub from Claude's connectors, or use GitHub's official MCP server (github.com/github/github-mcp-server). Help: support.claude.com (search "connectors").
- GitHub Copilot: reads the repo natively. Docs: docs.github.com/copilot. Microsoft 365 Copilot is a different product and doesn't read the repo by default.

## 7. Token hygiene and 2FA (offer, keep short)
- Review grants at GitHub, Settings, Applications, Authorized OAuth Apps. Repo access is broad: usually every repo they can reach. Revoke anything unfamiliar (only after their yes if you do it).
- Password manager (1Password, or Bitwarden as open-source) with unique passwords everywhere.
- 2FA everywhere, passkeys or authenticator app over SMS; backup codes in the password manager.
- Revocation: GitHub Settings, Applications; ChatGPT Settings, Apps & Connectors; each platform's connector settings. Grants last until revoked, so one breached platform can reach everything connected.

## 8. Data and privacy (a real choice)
Connected files can end up in prompts, caches, summaries and provider processing. Keep the repo private, no secrets or personal data in files (use environment variables or a secrets manager), prefer connectors with clear retention policies, and periodically check what each platform can access.

## 9. Pacing (background)
GitHub allows about 5,000 authenticated requests an hour and limits content creation (roughly 80 a minute, 500 an hour). On a 429, or a 403 with no remaining quota, wait for the reset time or Retry-After, then retry with backoff. Push files a few at a time.

## 10. Verify and hand off
Optional check: have them ask a second AI to read STATE.md. Then tell them the repo is the shared source of truth: any AI should read AGENTS.md and STATE.md first and update HANDOFF.md before ending a session. Optionally offer a quarterly grant-review reminder; never turn it on without their yes.
